claims.measured: Start-up: node-express 706 ms, node-fastify 593 ms vs csharp-aspnet 785 ms
claims.why: Both Node servers started faster than ASP.NET Core in the measurements, so the direction is right.

claims.claim: Node's start-up advantage over .NET is typically a few hundred milliseconds to a second or so
claims.about: Node.js vs .NET cold start on Azure Functions
claims.measured: Start-up gap for standalone servers: 79 ms (Express) to 192 ms (Fastify)
claims.why: The figure is about cold starts inside the Azure Functions host and worker, which weren't measured; the plain-container gap measured is smaller (80–190 ms), so if anything the claim leans high.

claims.claim: Go would have a start-up advantage, but as a Functions custom handler it gives up much of that advantage
claims.about: Go vs .NET start-up on Azure Functions
claims.measured: Start-up: go-nethttp 238 ms, go-gin 293 ms vs csharp-aspnet 785 ms
claims.why: The measurements back the implied point that Go starts faster than .NET as a standalone server, but they don't cover Go running as an Azure Functions custom handler, so the loss of that advantage can't be checked.

claims.claim: Native AOT gives the fastest .NET startup
claims.why: Only one .NET setup (ASP.NET Core) was measured, with no Native AOT or ReadyToRun build to compare against.
